cards.text: Paul is writing to the church in Corinth about a gift they're collecting for believers in need, and Titus, one of his coworkers, is part of the plan. Right here, Paul stops to thank God for something He put into Titus's heart.

cards.question: Paul thanks God for what He put into Titus's heart for the Corinthians. What is it?

answers.text: The same devotion Paul has for them
A wish to lead their church himself
A worry about how they'd been giving

cards.question: Paul made an appeal to Titus about this trip. True or false: Titus is only heading to Corinth because Paul made him go.

cards.text: Of his own volition! Paul asks for a favor, and Titus is already standing by the door with his bag packed.
And Titus gets company for the road. Paul's sending a brother with him who's praised by ALL the churches, not some, ALL of them!

cards.question: The brother traveling with Titus is praised by all the churches for his work in the ___.

cards.text: More than that, the churches CHOSE this brother to travel with Paul's team and the gracious offering they administer to honor the Lord Himself. Hand-picked by the churches, friend, and me, I got picked out of a bargain bin for a quarter!

cards.question: Paul's team is handling a generous gift from the churches. What does Paul want to avoid?

answers.text: Any criticism of how it's handled
Any delay in getting it delivered
Any churches finding out about it

cards.question: True or false: Paul says doing right in the Lord's eyes is all that matters, and what people see doesn't count.

cards.text: Paul wants it done right in the Lord's eyes AND in people's eyes. With a generous gift being handled, folks watch close, like I watch the oven in the last thirty seconds of a batch: no blinking, no talking, NO breathing.
And one more man joins the trip: another brother who has proven his earnestness to Paul many times and in many ways. Not once, not twice, MANY times, friend!

cards.question: Paul says this other brother is proving his earnestness even more now. How?

answers.text: By his great confidence in the Corinthians
By paying his own way to Corinth
By leaving his home to travel

cards.text: Now Paul makes the introductions like a proud dad at a work party. Titus is his partner and fellow worker among the Corinthians, and I bet Paul's grinning ear to ear writing that.

cards.question: And the brothers traveling with Titus? Paul calls them ___ of the churches.

cards.text: Paul even calls those brothers the glory of Christ. So when they arrive, the Corinthians have something to show them, in full view of the churches.

cards.question: When Paul's team arrives in Corinth, what does Paul want the Corinthians to show them in front of the churches?

cards.text: Now Paul turns to the gift itself, the service to the saints. Pull up a stool, friend.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says he needs to write the Corinthians all about the service to the saints.
Paul says there's no need to write the Corinthians about the gift. Why not?

answers.text: He knows how eager they are to help
He covered it all in an earlier letter

cards.text: In fact, Paul's been bragging about them to the Macedonians, the believers over in Macedonia. He's told them the Corinthians in Achaia have been prepared to give since last year!

cards.question: Paul says the zeal of the Corinthians has ___ most of the Macedonians to do likewise.

cards.text: The Corinthians' zeal stirred most of those Macedonians to do the same! It's like one person jumping up for a standing ovation, and suddenly most of the room is on its feet.

cards.question: Paul's been boasting that the Corinthians are ready to give. So why is he still sending the brothers?

answers.text: So his boasting won't prove empty
So he can ask for a bigger gift
So they can check on the teaching

cards.text: Paul wants them prepared, just like he said. It's like promising a friend the cookie box is packed and ready, and when that friend shows up, that box had better be FULL.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says if Macedonians come with him and find the Corinthians unprepared, only the Corinthians would be ashamed.

cards.text: Paul says he and his team would be ashamed of having been so confident, to say nothing of the Corinthians. Ask me how I know: I once bragged that my next batch would be my best EVER, then opened the oven and just stood there on my gold base for a LONG time.

cards.question: So Paul urges the brothers to go on ahead and arrange the gift the Corinthians promised. How does he want that gift to be prepared?

answers.text: Quietly and not in public view

cards.text: Generously, not begrudgingly! Nobody wants a cookie handed over with a heavy sigh and a mumbled "fine, here, take it."
